suggested_services_note: Each row is one way this kind of work takes money (one of the master's 28 paths per flow). The owner keeps the services that fit and picks ONE path per service and place. Names and amounts are examples from the profession file, not prices.

suggested_services.name: Assessment
suggested_services.example: The main story: an assessment, then weekly visits. Nothing taken when booking; the plan is billed, and any share is paid at the front desk. The free screening call also runs here, with nothing to pay.

suggested_services.name: Assessment
suggested_services.example: A sliding-fee visit, or a share billed after the plan pays.

suggested_services.name: Individual visit
suggested_services.example: A self-pay visit: a card is saved, nothing is taken, and the visit is charged to the saved card when the counselor marks it DONE. A late-cancel fee applies only if it was agreed at booking and the owner confirms.

suggested_services.name: Court-ordered class series
suggested_services.example: A court-ordered education class series, $250, paid in full when booking. Nothing more is charged after it.

suggested_services.name: Home-based visit
suggested_services.example: The main story: a home-based visit with David, Thu Oct 22 at 8:00am. Nothing is taken; the plan is billed, and any share is texted as a bill after the visit.

suggested_services.name: Home-based visit
suggested_services.example: The same visit for a publicly funded client: nothing is taken and no card is saved; the program bills the public funder its own way.

suggested_services.name: Home-based visit
suggested_services.example: A self-pay home visit: a card is saved, and the visit is charged to it at DONE. A late-cancel fee applies only if agreed at booking and the owner confirms.

before_times: what it's for: a screening call, an assessment, a session, a group or intensive outpatient, a family session, a medication visit, or a court-ordered assessment or class
a health plan, self-pay (the sliding fee), or public funding (only the name here)
whether a court, a probation officer, an employer or a licensing board requires it (sets the kind of assessment; who it is and the papers go on the secure page)
for a group: which days work
the client's age (adolescent and adult groups are separate)
after_time: the safe way to reach them (a shared phone?)
the plain name they want on texts
secure_page_only: the screening questions: what is used, how often, past treatment, and withdrawal signs (to see whether a detox program is needed first)
the plan's member details, or income for the sliding fee (proof only here)

consents: treatment consent, the privacy notice for addiction treatment records (a stricter federal rule), and each release the client chooses, naming who may be told what and until when (a court, a probation officer, an employer, a family member)
the group agreement: other members' names and stories stay private
for a minor: the parent's consent, or the minor's own consent where the state's rules allow it
intake_questions.who_may_book: an adult books for themselves; a family member may ask for someone, but the client books and consents on their own link; a court or employer may require the visit but never books it or learns anything without the client's signed release naming them; where the state lets a minor consent to addiction treatment, the minor may book alone and the parent isn't told without the minor's yes (a switch from the state form); otherwise a parent or guardian consents

stop.say: If you're thinking about harming yourself, call or text 988 now. If you're in danger right now, call 911.
stop.booking: 988 and 911 first, at once, any hour; no booking in that chat until a clear 'I'm safe right now'; the counselor is told privately the same day

stop.words: an overdose: not breathing, blue lips, won't wake up
stop.say: Call 911 now. If you have naloxone, use it.

stop.words: dangerous withdrawal: a seizure, confusion, seeing things, shaking with a fever
stop.say: Call 911 or go to the emergency room now.

stop.words: harming someone else, or anyone in danger right now
stop.say: This sounds like an emergency. If anyone is in danger, get to safety and call 911 now.
stop.booking: no booking; the program's own person is told at once, any hour

go_on.words: drinks heavily every day or takes sedatives daily and gets shaky when stopping, or asks for detox
go_on.what: the assessment is booked only after the program's nurse or counselor reads the screening (stopping alcohol or sedatives suddenly can be dangerous); Rosie gives the program's line and never advises stopping or cutting down
never a reason to refuse; the counselor is told privately; the booking goes on
never answered by Rosie: the prescriber

go_on.words: not safe at home, or domestic violence
go_on.what: 911 if in danger now; the national hotline; reached only the safe way they pick

safety_and_stop_words.always: the generic screen: danger to life, fire, gas, a medical emergency → call 911, and no booking

first_steps_and_forms.prep: for the reminder: photo ID, the plan card, any court or referral papers; come 15 minutes early for the first visit

staff.skills: addiction counselor, clinical counselor or social worker, prescriber, adolescent groups, family sessions, intensive outpatient, approved court-ordered assessments and classes, home-based sessions, Spanish
staff.licenses_or_certificates: each counselor's credential and level; each prescriber's license and federal registration
staff.supervision: trainees, and credential levels the state requires, work only under a named clinical supervisor
staff.who_oks: the clinical supervisor OKs a change in level of care and any client flagged for detox; the owner OKs fees, refunds and the sliding fee
staff.stand_in: individual sessions: another counselor only with the client's yes; groups: any counselor with the skill (a group isn't booked by name); a court-ordered assessment: only an approved counselor

children_and_age.who_may_book: an adult books for themselves; a family member may ask for someone, but the client books and consents on their own link; a court or employer may require the visit but never books it or learns anything without the client's signed release naming them; where the state lets a minor consent to addiction treatment, the minor may book alone and the parent isn't told without the minor's yes (a switch from the state form); otherwise a parent or guardian consents
children_and_age.minors_texts: a minor who consents for themselves gets their own texts; a parent gets texts only with the minor's yes where the state's rules let the minor consent

visit.check_in: the code at the front desk or with the counselor; groups: the counselor ticks the roster on the secure page (members never see who's booked); by video: the code read at the start
visit.done: the code or the roster tick, then DONE; clinical notes, drug screen results, attendance letters and court reports stay in the program's own records and go out only with a signed release naming the recipient; Rosie keeps only booking records
visit.changes_at_visit: the counselor may change the level of care (more or less intensive): booked as its own plan with the client's yes; a drug screen at a session is part of treatment, never a separate sale

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: the program's own word, optional: the program's state license or certification for outpatient substance use treatment, if it has one; each counselor's own credential or clinical license, as the owner gives it; a prescriber's license for medication visits. Rosie never looks a license up and never says one is checked
license.who: both: the program and each counselor and prescriber
license.ask: the program's license or certification number and its levels of care (outpatient, intensive outpatient); each counselor's credential, its level and their clinical supervisor; each prescriber's license and federal registration; any state or court approval to give court-ordered or driving-under-the-influence assessments and classes
license.insurance: professional liability insurance where the state's form asks for it
license.background: background checks for staff in adolescent programs, where the state's rules require them

never_in_a_text: that the person is in addiction treatment, what is used, drug screen results, diagnoses, medicines, court or probation details, and money details never go in a text, a voicemail or an answer to another AI: only the secure page; texts use the program's plain display name (never 'recovery' or 'addiction'), the day, the time and the place
